posts.title: Gleam Resources
posts.description: A friendly language for building type-safe systems on the Erlang VM. I'm currently using it to learn networking from the TCP layer up. Gleam is the first language in a while that made me want to write a network service for the joy of it. The type system is small. The syntax is calm. posts.title: Retro: Building an SMTP Server in Gleam - Part 1
posts.description: I've been building an SMTP server in Gleam lately. I won't say "From scratch" as I'm using Rawhat's wonderful Glisten library, which provides the TCP transport layer, but outside of that, I'm not (currently) using any other libraries. posts.title: Interfaces in Zig
posts.description: Zig does not have an interface keyword — and that’s a feature, not a bug. Zig’s design deliberately avoids baking object-oriented abstractions into the language. Instead, it gives you a small set of powerful primitives — structs, pointers, comptime, and function pointers — and lets you decide when abstraction is worth the cost.
